rubric.reason: Independently reproduced, not taken on trust. (1) vi.mock cross-module interception: a temporary throwaway repro file (created and deleted, no residual diff) confirmed that `vi.mock("../src/worker/push/send", ...)` registered in a test file does NOT intercept src/worker/cron.ts's own static `import { sendPush } from "./push/send"` in the @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers pool: calling `sendModule.sendPush` via a fresh `await import(...)` in the test file resolved to the mock (toString showed the mock arrow function), but invoking `runScheduledJob(env)` — which calls sendPush only through cron.ts's own already-bound import — left the mock at 0 calls and left the seeded Reminder's `sentAt` reset to null (the retryable-release path), i.e. the REAL sendPush ran, threw internally on the fixture's non-base64 'fake-p256dh'/'fake-auth' keys, and classifyPushOutcome swallowed it as retryable. Running the actual test/cron-reminder-route.test.ts unmodified reproduces the same 'expected 1, got 0' failure on both its assertions. This holds despite test/cron-heartbeat.test.ts's header describing vi.mock as working for 'cross-module namespace imports' (only self-import is called out there as broken) — that framing does not generalize to this nested (test -> cron.ts -> push/send.ts) case, and the codebase's own prior art agrees: test/cron-sweep.test.ts, written earlier for the same runScheduledJob/sendPush pair, deliberately stubs at the global `fetch` level instead of mocking the push/send module, for exactly this reason. (2) AC-8 is satisfied by production code: read src/worker/cron.ts:57-64 and src/shared/app-route.ts directly — route is `pathOf(taskRouteOf(reminder.taskId))` when `reminder.taskId !== null`, else '/', which is exactly PRD AC-8's (PRPs/prds/reminders.prd.md:152-156) required shape, and a separate repro confirmed vi.spyOn(sendModule,'sendPush') captures cron.ts's real plaintext payload argument (`{"data":{"route":"/"}}` for a standalone Reminder), proving the route value observed is cron.ts's own computed value, not an artifact of the broken mock. (3) `npm run check` in the CODE ROOT reproduces TS2556 at test/cron-reminder-route.test.ts(48,50) — 'A spread argument must either have a tuple type or be passed to a rest parameter' — on the `(...args: unknown[]) => sendPushMock(...args)` factory body; the error is inside the APPROVED test file, zero production files touched. (4) A vi.spyOn-based rewrite preserves the original assertion's force: a repro using `import * as sendModule from "../src/worker/push/send"; vi.spyOn(sendModule, "sendPush").mockResolvedValue(...)` DID intercept cron.ts's call (spy.mock.calls.length === 1) and captured the exact plaintext JSON payload string cron.ts builds — the same second argument `parsedPayloadFromCall` already parses — so `expect(payload.data.route).toBe(expectedPath)` retains identical discriminating power and would still fail against a cron.ts hardcoded to route:'/' for a Task-linked Reminder. Verdict: the test's ASSERTIONS correctly express AC-8 and must not change; only its MOCKING MECHANISM is defective and must change.

dispute_evidence.claim: The test asserts, via `expect(sendPushMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)`, that `vi.mock("../src/worker/push/send", () => ({ sendPush: (...args) => sendPushMock(...args) }))` intercepts src/worker/cron.ts's `import { sendPush } from "./push/send"`. The implementer instrumented cron.ts (temporarily, then reverted) and found `sendPush` still resolves to the real `[AsyncFunction: sendPush]` in this @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers pool. The real function then runs against the fixture's `p256dh: "fake-p256dh"` / `auth: "fake-auth"`, throws internally on `atob()` invalid base64, `classifyPushOutcome` swallows it as `{ ok: false, error }`, and sendPushMock is legitimately never called — so the assertion fails for a reason unrelated to the route. The implementer then printed the actual payload built at cron.ts:57-64 (no mock involved) and observed `{"data":{"route":"/tasks/<taskId>"}}` for the Task-linked fixture and `{"data":{"route":"/"}}` for the standalone one, i.e. AC-8 is satisfied by cron.ts:61. Separately, test/cron-reminder-route.test.ts:48 fails `tsc -b` with TS2556 (spread argument must have a tuple type or be passed to a rest parameter) on `sendPushMock(...args)` — a compile defect inside the APPROVED test file itself.
dispute_evidence.proposed_resolution: Amend the test to use `import * as sendModule from "../src/worker/push/send"` + `vi.spyOn(sendModule, "sendPush")`, mirroring test/cron-heartbeat.test.ts's documented pattern for this exact pool, which also resolves the TS2556 typing defect. cron.ts:61 needs no change.

arbitration_directive.test_writer_must_change: Replace the top-level `vi.mock("../src/worker/push/send", () => ({ sendPush: (...args: unknown[]) => sendPushMock(...args) }))` (lines 45-49) with `import * as sendModule from "../src/worker/push/send";` plus, inside each `it` (or a shared `beforeEach`), `const sendPushMock = vi.spyOn(sendModule, "sendPush").mockResolvedValue({ ok: true, statusCode: 201 });` — mirroring test/cron-heartbeat.test.ts's documented vi.spyOn-on-namespace pattern for this pool. This also removes the TS2556 compile error at line 48, since vi.spyOn's return type is correctly inferred without a manual spread wrapper.
arbitration_directive.test_writer_must_not_change: Every assertion: `expect(sendPushMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)`, `parsedPayloadFromCall`'s parsing of `call[1]`, `expect(payload.data.route).toBe(expectedPath)` (Task-linked case), the AC-8 round-trip assertion `expect(pathOf(routeFromPath(payload.data.route))).toBe(payload.data.route)`, and `expect(payload.data.route).toBe("/")` (standalone case). None of these were shown to be wrong; only the interception mechanism was. No change to src/worker/cron.ts, src/shared/app-route.ts, or any other production file.
